method: Read the source of AI_PUZZLE_TRACK, AI_WHEEL (with AI_WHEEL_COLOURS) and HEALTH_CHAT in both versions (not the bench, the earlier review fixtures for 1.24.20, the generator of the sixth review, or the 1.24.20 changelog). Booted src/lantern.inner.html (1.24.20 draft) and scratchpad inner_1_24_19.html (1.24.19) in Node + jsdom as given. Wrote 368 cases of my own (220 TRACK, 44 wheel, 104 bites), worked each answer out by hand before running, ran each on both versions and timed it. Rule 1 verdicts: right = the hand answer (or a stated alternative, or a problem where a question back is fair); missed = a right input sent back as a problem; spoiled = a right input answered with a different row or holders; mended-wrong = a wrong or loose input answered silently instead of asked; crash = an exception. Rule 3: right = one part per colour in the hand order, or left as written where that is right; missed = left in groups (or sent back) where the question asks for a plain colour wheel; spoiled = groups the question asks for turned into hue wedges; mended-wrong = wedges in another order or set. Rule 5 (every question is one a person could ask): right = the Bites and stings lesson exactly when a person was bitten or stung; missed = a bite to a person without it; spoiled = the lesson (with Chat's 'this is a health question, give the steps to do now') for a question that is not one. newIn_1_24_20 = 1.24.20's outcome differs from 1.24.19's (answer, holders, wheel parts, or whether the Bites lesson is sent). Random TRACK scripts: a generator of my own (scratchpad gen.js, seeded) with its own simulator, rows of 3 to 7 people or cups, 2 to 7 lines each from: swap (by name, position, ordinal, second to last, k-th from either end, left/right/behind/in front of a place, the one between, the holder of, next to an end), give/put, pass (k places), swap contents, move to first/last/position/second to last, move before/after a place, move k places, shift/rotate, reverse, add (front, back, position, before/after a place, between), remove, take from, swap two held things, two steps joined by then (5 joiners), and a step repeated (twice, 2 times, two times, 3 times, three times, thrice). 4000 plain scripts (seeds 7001..11000) and 3000 with harder forms (seeds 90001..93000: move the one holding/with/that has X before/after a place, swap X and the one to its left/on its right, give X from <holder> to <place>, pass it to the one behind the one holding it, the one k places to the left of, the one at the front). Plain: 1.24.20 {"right":3700,"missed":300}, 1.24.19 {"right":244,"missed":3480,"spoiled":276}; every 1.24.20 miss is 'move X left of / right of P' (not in the grammar; 1.24.19 the same). Harder: 1.24.20 {"right":2943,"spoiled":29,"missed":28}, 1.24.19 {"spoiled":197,"missed":2632,"right":171}; the first wrong line of each failing script is one of two forms: 'move <the one/cup/person holding|with|that has X> before/after/behind <a place with to, at or in in it>' (11 right, 18 silently wrong, 15 sent back, of the 44 that were reached) and 'give X from the back to <place>' (2 right, 12 silently wrong: a new thing 'X from' is made). Line by line every other form was right on every line reached. Time (1.24.20): the largest TRACK run was 9 ms over all cases and the 7000 scripts (mean 0.13 to 0.16 ms; each set of scripts under 1 s); a 5000-name row 44 ms; places nested 9 and 40 deep, 30 ands, 25 tos, 12 thens, 100 repeats, 40 ofs: each 0 to 14 ms; a wheel build up to 18 ms; the first healthLessons call about 170 to 190 ms (the lesson index), the rest under 30 ms. No crash, no hang, nothing over a second.
